title: What to watch tomorrow morning
text: Tech bounced back on Tuesday. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 0.6% to $685.28 and the S&P 500 fund SPY rose 0.3% to $754.42. Among Nasdaq companies, industrial and real estate firms did best, and tech rose about 0.9%. Tomorrow morning, watch how AMD trades after its results, because chip stocks often move together. Also watch the Treasury's borrowing announcement on Wednesday. One good day does not erase Monday's drop. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Big tech and chip stocks rebounded
text: Vertiv rose 5.2% to $235.99, Rocket Lab rose 4.5% to $54.43, Microsoft rose 2.7% to $520.99, Meta rose 2.4% to $621.03, Nvidia rose 2.3% to $206.69 and Amazon rose 2.1% to $250.69. These are the same kinds of companies that fell on Monday. Prices that swing both ways like this are what we call volatile.

title: AMD closed higher before its report
text: AMD rose 3.7% to $483.90 before the market closed. The company said it would share its third quarter results after the close, and it had told investors to expect about $13 billion in sales. The price can jump or drop tomorrow based on how the real numbers compare with what people hoped for. We did not have the results yet when this was written.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield edged up
text: The 10 year Treasury yield, the interest the government pays to borrow for ten years, was 4.95% on Tuesday, up from 4.91% on Monday. It is still below the 5.05% it hit on October 28. When this rate is high, safer investments pay more, and growth stocks can feel the pressure.

title: Steady names lagged the rally
text: The dividend fund SCHD fell 1.0% to $35.54 and Lockheed Martin fell 0.6% to $639.19, while fast growing companies rose. Calmer companies often move less on big up days, and they also tend to fall less on down days.

title: Lesson 35: What is after-hours trading?
text: The regular stock market opens at 9:30 in the morning and closes at 4:00 in the afternoon, New York time. But some trading also happens before the open and after the close. That is called extended hours or after-hours trading. Companies often share their results right after the close, so prices can move fast in the evening. There are fewer buyers and sellers then, so prices can jump around more and be harder to get at a fair price. That is why many learners wait for the next regular open before reacting to news. This is education, not advice.
